records.title: Incidence of Decompression Illness and Subjective Efficacy of Hypoxia Training With and Without O2 Pre-Breathing in Singapore
records.locator: Aerospace Medicine and Human Performance 89(3), 171–172, AsMA abstract 038
records.evidence_note: The two policy periods have identical exposure and case totals to Cheok et al. (2021). The abstract calls the four diagnoses decompression sickness and describes joint pain in all cases and no neurologic symptoms. The later article labels the diagnoses decompression illness and describes persistent limb numbness in one case. The two reports share a cohort, and the difference in symptom description is retained.

records.title: A Rare Complication of Hypobaric Hypoxia Training
records.locator: Aerospace Medicine and Human Performance 89(3), 171, AsMA abstract 037
records.evidence_note: Two aircrew developed symptoms during or shortly after hypobaric chamber decompression in routine physiological training. The presenter reports a clinical diagnosis of cerebral arterial gas embolism for both. The abstract gives no participant-exposure denominator or case dates. Dhahran, Saudi Arabia is the presenting affiliation, and the abstract supplies no separately named site.

records.title: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Decompression Sickness in Altitude Physiological Training
records.locator: Aerospace Medicine and Human Performance 89(3), 171, AsMA abstract 036
records.evidence_note: The abstract reports the same JSC cohort period and six student cases in 9,560 exposures as the journal review. It separately identifies one trainer with pain-only DCS and gives no trainer exposure total. Its meta-analysis profile count and numerical summaries are preserved as abstract-level results.

note: Re-read the primary report in the publication and verified the archived PDF checksum against the existing outcome extraction.

records.title: Decompression Illness Incidence and Hypoxia Symptoms After Prebreathing in Hypobaric Hypoxia Training
records.locator: Aerospace Medicine and Human Performance 92(5), 289–293, Methods and Results p. 290, Limitations p. 292
records.evidence_note: The duty aeromedical specialist diagnosed decompression illness using training and medical records. Symptoms in the first policy period were reported after training, and the second-period cases presented during training. One second-period case had limb numbness plus digit symptoms. Some people trained in both periods. The paper gives no separate staff margins or standardized delayed surveillance interval. The existing v1 outcome rows use these same policy periods and exposure counts.
